q-61724.name: Question 1
q-61724.worked_solution:
We substitute $x=4$ and $g(x)=3$ into the expression for $g(x)$ and solve for $M,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3 & =M\cdot {(\frac{1}{2})}^{4} \\ 3 & =M\cdot (\frac{{1}^{4}}{{2}^{4}}) \\ 3 & =M\cdot \frac{1}{16} \\ 3\cdot 16 & =M \\ 48 & =M\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $M=48.$

q-112141.name: Question 2
q-112141.problem: The growth of a mice colony is given by the formula $M(t)=6\cdot {2}^{t},$ where $t$ is the time, in months, since the beginning of the observation. How many mice will the colony have after $5$ months?
q-112141.worked_solution:
To get the number of mice in the colony after $5$ months, we evaluate the function at $t=5.$ Substituting $t=5$ into the function $M(t)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}M(5) & =6\cdot {2}^{5} \\  & =6\cdot 32 \\  & =192.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, after $5$ months there will be $192$ mice in the colony.

q-218599.worked_solution:
We substitute $x=4$ and $f(x)=2$ into the expression for $f(x)$ and solve for $A,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =A\cdot {(\frac{1}{3})}^{4} \\ 2 & =A\cdot (\frac{{1}^{4}}{{3}^{4}}) \\ 2 & =A\cdot \frac{1}{81} \\ 2\cdot 81 & =A \\ 162 & =A\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $A=162.$
